content:
Fractions in Class 4 stretch to improper fractions, mixed numbers, simplest form and comparisons — a favourite Olympiad hunting ground. This guide explains what the Maths Olympiad Class 4 fractions chapter tests, the key ideas, the traps, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 4 Maths Olympiad Fractions chapter tests

  • Proper, improper and mixed fractions (conversions both ways)
  • Equivalent fractions and simplest form
  • Comparing and ordering fractions
  • Adding/subtracting like fractions and fraction of a number

Key facts your child should know

  • 7/4 = 1 3/4 because 7 ÷ 4 = 1 remainder 3.
  • Simplest form: divide top and bottom by their HCF — 8/12 = 2/3.
  • Same numerator → the smaller denominator is the bigger fraction.
  • 3/4 of 20 = 20 ÷ 4 × 3 = 15.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Adding denominators when adding like fractions.
  • Leaving an answer unsimplified when simplest form is asked.
  • Flipping the comparison for same-numerator fractions.

quiz.title: IMO Class 4 Fractions Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: A train has completed 4/7 of its journey. What fraction of the journey is still remaining?
Which of the following is a proper fraction?
questions.explanation: In 3/8 the numerator 3 is less than the denominator 8, so it is a proper fraction.

questions.q: 4 2/5 is the same as which improper fraction?
questions.explanation: Multiply the whole part by the denominator and add the numerator: 4 x 5 + 2 = 22, so 4 2/5 = 22/5.
Multiply the whole part by the denominator and add the numerator: 3 x 6 + 1 = 19, so 3 1/6 = 19/6.

questions.q: Aman ate 5/12 of a chocolate bar. What fraction of the bar is left?
Sonal painted 3/10 of a wall before lunch and 4/10 after lunch. What fraction of the wall did she paint in total?
questions.explanation: Same denominators, so add numerators: 3 + 4 = 7, giving 7/10.

questions.q: A jar is 1/6 full of sugar. Another 5/18 of the jar is filled. What fraction of the jar is now full, in simplest form?

questions.explanation: The denominators are the same, so add the numerators: 1 + 5 = 6, giving 6/8 = 3/4 in simplest form.

questions.q: 2/5 = 8/?. Which number goes in place of the question mark?
questions.explanation: The numerator 2 was multiplied by 4 to get 8, so the denominator becomes 5 x 4 = 20.
The denominator 9 was multiplied by 3 to get 27, so the numerator becomes 2 x 3 = 6.

faq.q: How do you convert an improper fraction to a mixed number?
faq.a: Divide the top by the bottom: the quotient is the whole part and the remainder sits over the same denominator. 11/4 = 2 3/4.
A fraction whose top and bottom share no common factor except 1 — divide both by their HCF to get it.
